messages.author: e26511c35c7ed172
messages.subject: mod_R.so and libR.dylib don't load
parts:
Hi,

after upgrading R, my local web-server doesn't run, the Apache doesn't
restart.

For testing I left in 'httpd.conf' only 2 lines which are rApache
related:

LoadModule R_module libexec/apache2/mod_R.so
ROutputErrors


Here what I get as error message:

$ sudo apachectl -k restart
httpd: Syntax error on line 118 of /private/etc/apache2/httpd.conf:
Cannot load /usr/libexec/apache2/mod_R.so into server: dlopen(/usr/
libexec/apache2/mod_R.so, 10): Library not loaded: /Library/Frameworks/
R.framework/Versions/2.13/Resources/lib/libR.dylib\n Referenced
from: /usr/libexec/apache2/mod_R.so\n Reason: image not found

Here some info about R:

R version 2.14.1 (2011-12-22)
Copyright (C) 2011 The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
ISBN 3-900051-07-0
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin9.8.0/x86_64 (64-bit)

$ lipo -info /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/lib/libR.dylib
Architectures in the fat file: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/
Resources/lib/libR.dylib are: ppc7400 x86_64 i386

$ ls -la /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/
total 8
drwxrwxr-x 4 root admin 136 Jan 10 22:41 .
drwxrwxr-x 8 root admin 272 Jan 10 22:41 ..
drwxrwxr-x 6 root admin 204 Jan 10 22:41 2.14
lrwxr-xr-x 1 root admin 4 Jan 10 22:41 Current -> 2.14

Any comments would be highly appreciated,
Maciej

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: mod_R.so and libR.dylib don't load
parts:
I've just verified that your REvalOnStartup line works on my system.
You need to reconcile your .libPath() directories in rApache and R. To
do this:

1. Take out the offending REvalOnStartup line, then start rApache with
the r-info directive on and take note of the .libPaths() output. It's
a link on the left-hand side of the r-info output page.
2. Run R from the command line (the exact R that you used to compile
rApache) and then print out .libPaths().

See if there's a difference in the two. (cc'ing the list as this may
be helpful advice to other users).

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: mod_R.so and libR.dylib don't load
parts:
On Tue, Jan 17, 2012 at 12:30 AM, Paul Gleichauf
<paul.gl...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Jeff,
>
> Again thanks for the quick turnaround. You provided an important hint that
> enabled me to solve the problems I was having.
>
> There is a difference between the two paths:
>
> RApacheInfo returns one entry:
>
> /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.14/Resources/library
>
> The R terminal at /usr/bin/R64 returns two entries:
>
>> .libPaths()
> [1] "/Users/gleichauf/Library/R/2.14/library"
> [2] "/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.14/Resources/library"
>
> This behavior is based upon installing an R binary image.
>
> I have been worried for a while why RApacheInfo did not show the packages I
> had installed. Now I see by looking at the two directories above that only
> the first in the pair holds packages I have installed, and RApacheInfo is
> looking at the second. In addition
>
> http://CRAN.R-project.org/bin/macosx/RMacOSX-FAQ.html#R-and-external-applications
>
> says to remove the first (user-specific) directory before upgrades. So I
> reinstalled R entirely and took care when installing packages to use the
> <lib> option in install-packages(packages-character-vector>,<lib>,...) to
> include the second Frameworks directory above. Now RApacheInfo shows the
> installed packages as expected.
>
>  When it came to getting brew running after RApache, I had some confusion
> about when an absolute path (<Directory> is required and when a relative one
> suffices <Location> based solely on the RApache documentation.  It is also

Actually, <Directory> is a directive that lays down rules for physical
files on the disk, while <Location> is a directive that sets rules for
URL space... there are no files. Let me know if there's some
improvements I can make to section "3.6.1 Difference in Location and
Directory" in the manual. I understand it's confusing.

Jeff

> worth noting that on OSX server Apache is used somewhat differently than on
> Linux. Tthere can be some challenges getting the default directory location
> set in the Server administration tool that makes changes to several files
> when the server is started, including httpd.conf. See for
> example: http://CRAN.R-project.org/bin/macosx/RMacOSX-FAQ.html#R-and-external-applications
>
> Once the first samples are running things become so much simpler...
>
> Paul
>
